| Airline | Average departure delay | Departures delayed **>15 minutes** | Departures analyzed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| United (UA) | **12.67 min** | **20.45%** | 5,056 |
| Alaska (AS) | **10.60 min** | **21.39%** | 1,019 |
| Delta (DL) | **14.00 min** | **23.61%** | 1,224 |
| Southwest (WN) | **21.84 min** | **37.77%** | 699 |

**Exactly where these came from:** BTS TranStats → Airline On-Time Statistics → [Detailed Statistics: Departures](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ontime/Departures.aspx). I selected **Origin Airport = SFO; July; all days 1–31; 2025**, separately for **UA, AS, DL and WN**, and exported the CSV field **“Departure delay (Minutes).”** I removed flights listed in BTS’s [Detailed Statistics: Cancellation](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ontime/Cancellation.aspx) with the same filters: 56 United, 22 Alaska, 9 Delta and 5 Southwest flights.

The average includes negative delays for early departures. The percentages are the number with delay **strictly greater than 15 minutes**, divided by the noncanceled flight counts above. These cover the named operating carriers’ domestic flights, excluding regional affiliates reported under separate carrier codes. See the [BTS dataset description](https://www.transtats.bts.gov/DatabaseInfo.asp?QO_VQ=EFD).

**Threshold note:** BTS normally defines a late departure as **15 minutes or more**. Using that definition, the shares are **21.28%, 21.98%, 24.26% and 39.63%**, respectively.

Suggested slide footnote: *Source: DOT/BTS TranStats, Airline On-Time Statistics, July 2025; SFO domestic departures by reporting operating carrier; cancellations excluded; calculations from flight-level records.*
